newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products boosted by local demand.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products boosted by local demand.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were supported by good demand and tight local supply on Tuesday, traders said.

Gas oil strengthened on local and eastern arbitrage interest. A Russian cargo was sold at high fob +$4.50, while one and possibly two further 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil parcels were sold out of Italy at between high fob +$4 and +$4.50.
"Gas oil is still very strong. Cargoes are moving quite quickly," a trader said.
Low sulphur diesel was seen possibly tightening under pressure from meagre supply but trade was inactive.
Gasoline was slightly stronger on relatively tight supply, but traders noted that demand remained relatively lacklustre.

Saudi Aramco was heard to have queried a handful of Mediterranean players about supplying 300,000 barrels in early May, but traders said it was unlikely it would be supplied out of the region because of the low level of the bid.
Traders said there were also small pockets of demand out of Turkey.
Naphtha remained tight but traders said demand for material was slight.

High sulphur fuel oil markets were actively talked, with good utility and bunker demand and traders believed to be positioning themselves for the results of the Portuguese tender, due out on Wednesday.
A major was heard to be offering $88 fob, well above market rates, for high sulphur material but turned down a cargo of good quality Turkish straight-run offered at the same price.

Brokers said there was a tussle on within the trade as to which direction the market should head. The low sulphur market was dull, with offers stable at around $101 cif and no trade seen. --London newsroom + 44 171 542 8060
